title: Three Texture Zeros in the Hermitian Dirac sector within Type-I Seesaw Mechanism
summary: We present numerical benchmark solutions for Hermitian Dirac neutrino mass matrices with three texture zeros within the type-I seesaw mechanism. The analysis is to normal ordering (NO) and inverted (IO). The heavy Majorana mass matrix is assumed diagonal, while the Dirac mass matrix is taken Hermitian. Four viable textures in NO are shown to reproduce the neutrino oscillation observables within the $3σ$ ranges of the NuFIT global analysis, and three viable textures in IO.

AI.tldr: The paper presents numerical benchmark solutions for Hermitian Dirac neutrino mass matrices with three texture zeros under the type-I seesaw mechanism, finding four viable textures for normal ordering (NO) and three for inverted ordering (IO) that reproduce neutrino oscillation data within 3σ ranges of NuFIT.
AI.motivation: To identify viable texture-zero structures in neutrino mass matrices that are consistent with current neutrino oscillation data, providing benchmark solutions within the type-I seesaw framework with Hermitian Dirac mass matrices and diagonal heavy Majorana mass matrices.
AI.method: The authors construct numerical benchmark solutions for Hermitian Dirac neutrino mass matrices featuring three texture zeros, assuming a type-I seesaw mechanism with a diagonal heavy Majorana mass matrix. The viable textures are tested against neutrino oscillation observables using NuFIT global analysis constraints at the 3σ confidence level for both normal and inverted mass orderings.
AI.result: Four viable textures for normal ordering (NO) and three viable textures for inverted ordering (IO) are found to reproduce the neutrino oscillation observables within the 3σ ranges of the NuFIT global analysis.
AI.conclusion: Only a limited set of texture-zero structures in Hermitian Dirac mass matrices can accommodate current neutrino oscillation data under the type-I seesaw mechanism, with more viable configurations allowed in normal ordering than in inverted ordering.

title: A regulated zero-temperature construction of the Fundamental Modular Region in pure Yang--Mills theory and QCD
summary: We formulate the Fundamental Modular Region (FMR) as the zero-temperature limit of regulated copy-weighted Landau gauges. At finite $β$, the measure localizes on absolute minima, and the leading correction is dominated by the inverse Faddeev--Popov (FP) operator. A small $SU(2)$ benchmark provides a computational realization through population annealing and collective basin hopping. Our construction defines absolute Landau gauge without parametrizing the FMR boundary and extends naturally to full quantum chromodynamics (QCD). It also admits a Hamiltonian interpretation in terms of the gauge-fixed vacuum wave functional on the FMR.

AI.tldr: This paper formulates the Fundamental Modular Region (FMR) as the zero-temperature limit of regulated copy-weighted Landau gauges, develops a computational realization via population annealing and collective basin hopping on a small SU(2) benchmark, and extends the construction to full QCD with a Hamiltonian interpretation in terms of the gauge-fixed vacuum wave functional.
AI.motivation: To define an absolute Landau gauge without needing to explicitly parametrize the FMR boundary, and to provide a computationally tractable and physically meaningful construction that extends to full QCD.
AI.method: The FMR is obtained as the zero-temperature limit of regulated copy-weighted Landau gauges. At finite β, the measure localizes on absolute minima with leading corrections dominated by the inverse Faddeev-Popov operator. A small SU(2) benchmark uses population annealing and collective basin hopping for computational realization.
AI.result: The construction provides an absolute Landau gauge without FMR boundary parametrization, successfully benchmarked on small SU(2), and extends naturally to full QCD with a Hamiltonian interpretation in terms of the gauge-fixed vacuum wave functional on the FMR.
AI.conclusion: The FMR can be rigorously and practically constructed via zero-temperature limits of regularized gauges, offering a boundary-free route to absolute Landau gauge fixing applicable to QCD, with a natural Hamiltonian interpretation.

title: LISA Reconstruction Landscape for Metastable Cosmic Strings
summary: We study reconstruction of stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds from metastable cosmic strings with the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). In the vacuum-tunneling benchmark, the network decays via zero-temperature nucleation of monopole pairs on the string worldsheet. Initially following cosmic-string scaling, loop production is suppressed after a decay time linked to efficient loop breaking and network collapse. This finite lifetime imprints an infrared tail and a transition toward a stable-string-like high-frequency plateau. Using synthetic LISA data with instrumental noise and unresolved astrophysical foregrounds, we perform Bayesian analysis in the $(Gμ,κ_{\rm CS})$ parameter space. We map detectability, uncertainties, correlations, and localization to distinguish background detection from parameter reconstruction. Reconstruction is governed by lifetime-dependent spectral features in the LISA band. When LISA samples the transition between tail and plateau, data contain amplitude and shape information, enabling recovery of string tension and metastability scale. Posteriors may remain correlated, reflecting an amplitude--lifetime trade-off, yet occupy a small parameter region. By contrast, featureless spectra constrain only limited parameter combinations or become prior dominated. High-SNR plateau-like spectra can retain partial sensitivity to $κ_{\rm CS}$ through residual lifetime dependence even when the transition is not prominent. Finally, we assess sensitivity to Galactic foreground modeling by comparing a flexible template with a reduced tanh template. Our results show where LISA can move beyond detection to probe the lifetime of the underlying string network.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the reconstruction of stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds (SGWB) generated by metastable cosmic strings using the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). Through Bayesian analysis in the (Gμ, κ_CS) parameter space using synthetic LISA data with instrumental noise and astrophysical foregrounds, the authors map detectability, parameter uncertainties, correlations, and localization across the parameter space, showing where LISA can move beyond detection to characterize the lifetime of the string network.
AI.motivation: Metastable cosmic strings are a compelling source of stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds potentially detectable by LISA. However, it is unclear whether LISA can not only detect such backgrounds but also reconstruct the underlying physical parameters (string tension and metastability scale), especially given that finite-lifetime effects imprint distinctive spectral features in the LISA band. Understanding where parameter reconstruction is feasible versus where only detection is possible is essential for planning and interpreting LISA observations.
AI.method: The authors generate synthetic LISA data for SGWBs from metastable cosmic strings in the vacuum-tunneling benchmark, where the network decays via zero-temperature nucleation of monopole pairs. They model the background with an infrared tail and a transition toward a stable-string-like high-frequency plateau, then perform Bayesian inference in the (Gμ, κ_CS) parameter space, including instrumental noise and unresolved astrophysical foregrounds. They assess reconstruction quality by mapping detectability, uncertainties, correlations, and localization, and compare a flexible Galactic foreground template with a reduced tanh template to test sensitivity to foreground modeling.
AI.result: Reconstruction quality is governed by lifetime-dependent spectral features in the LISA band. When the transition between tail and plateau is sampled, both amplitude and shape information are available, enabling recovery of string tension and metastability scale, though posteriors may remain correlated due to an amplitude–lifetime trade-off while still occupying a small parameter region. Featureless spectra only constrain limited parameter combinations or become prior-dominated. High-SNR plateau-like spectra can retain partial sensitivity to κ_CS through residual lifetime dependence even when the transition is not prominent. Sensitivity to Galactic foreground modeling was also assessed by comparing the two templates.
AI.conclusion: LISA can move beyond mere detection of metastable cosmic string backgrounds to reconstruct the lifetime of the underlying string network in regions of parameter space where the spectral transition falls within the LISA band. The work identifies specific observational windows where parameter recovery is feasible and delineates the limits of reconstruction for featureless or plateau-dominated spectra.

title: Generalized Kazakov-Migdal Models on Graphs via Artin-Ihara $L$-function and Random Partitions
summary: We introduce Kazakov-Migdal (KM)-type gauge theories on graphs via the Artin-Ihara $L$-function, providing a unified description of the models proposed in prior works. Using harmonic analysis on the group manifold, we reformulate the KM-type model on the cycle graph as a random partition model governed by the Schur measure. We exactly solve the KM-type model on the cycle graph in the fundamental representation as the random partition model in the large $N_c$ limit and demonstrate that the Gross-Witten-Wadia phase transition occurs precisely when the limiting shape of the Young diagram touches the boundary of the allowed representation space. We further clarify that this phase transition is intimately related to Bose-Einstein condensation, and the strong/weak coupling duality possesses a natural combinatorial interpretation as the exchange between the Young diagram and its complement, reflecting the functional equation of the Artin-Ihara $L$-function. We also establish a definitive relationship between the eigenvalue density of the unitary matrix and the Maya diagram density of the random partitions by deriving a droplet picture from the spectral curve.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Kazakov-Migdal-type gauge theories on graphs via the Artin-Ihara L-function, unifies previously proposed models, and exactly solves the cycle graph case in the fundamental representation as a random partition model governed by the Schur measure. The Gross-Witten-Wadia phase transition occurs when the limiting Young diagram touches the boundary of the allowed representation space, and is shown to be related to Bose-Einstein condensation. Strong/weak coupling duality corresponds to swapping the Young diagram with its complement, reflecting the functional equation of the Artin-Ihara L-function, and a droplet picture from the spectral curve connects eigenvalue density to Maya diagram density.

AI.method: The paper uses the Artin-Ihara L-function to define KM-type gauge theories on graphs, applies harmonic analysis on the group manifold to reformulate the cycle graph model as a random partition model governed by the Schur measure, and employs large N_c limit techniques to solve the model exactly.

title: Why 4D? Spontaneous Dimensional Selection from Gauge Criticality
summary: Noting that the Yang--Mills coupling is relevant below four dimensions, marginal in four dimensions, and irrelevant above four dimensions, I propose that this criticality can lead to the selection of four macroscopic dimensions. As a proof of principle, I present a concrete racetrack model of the type commonly studied in extra-dimensional scenarios, but without assuming a noncompact 4D spacetime. I find, within a well-controlled model without specifying the 4D, that 4D spacetime is spontaneously realized through radion stabilization via gauge-criticality-induced supersymmetry breaking and supergravity effects.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that the criticality of Yang-Mills coupling—relevant in d<4, marginal in d=4, irrelevant in d>4—can dynamically select four macroscopic spacetime dimensions. A racetrack model (typical in extra-dimensional scenarios) is presented without assuming a noncompact 4D spacetime, demonstrating that 4D is spontaneously realized via radion stabilization from gauge-criticality-induced supersymmetry breaking and supergravity effects.
AI.motivation: To understand why macroscopic spacetime is four-dimensional, rather than assuming 4D a priori. The author proposes a dynamical mechanism where the renormalization-group criticality of Yang-Mills coupling acts as a selection principle for spacetime dimensionality.
AI.method: The paper uses a racetrack model—a common construction in extra-dimensional scenarios—but crucially without pre-assuming a noncompact 4D spacetime. The approach relies on radion stabilization driven by gauge-criticality-induced supersymmetry breaking, combined with supergravity (gravity-mediated) effects to spontaneously realize 4D spacetime.
AI.result: Within a well-controlled model that does not specify the 4D a priori, it is found that 4D spacetime is spontaneously realized. The gauge-criticality mechanism (Yang-Mills being marginal in four dimensions) provides the dynamical selection pressure for four macroscopic dimensions through radion stabilization.
AI.conclusion: The criticality of Yang-Mills coupling near four dimensions can serve as a dynamical selection mechanism for macroscopic spacetime dimensionality, offering a proof-of-principle explanation for why we observe 4D spacetime via gauge-theoretic and supergravity dynamics rather than assuming it as a boundary condition.

title: Mega-Space Current Algebra and Green-Schwarz Geometry in Heterotic String Theory
summary: We study the Lorentz and gauge connections in heterotic string theories within a framework of manifest T-duality. A central motivation is the Bergshoeff--de Roo (BdR) type parallelism between the torsionful Lorentz and Yang-Mills connections in heterotic $α'$-corrections. We formulate worldsheet current algebras in a mega-space that incorporates the Lorentz and gauge sectors simultaneously. By generalizing the Poláček-Siegel scheme, we evaluate the commutators of the extended generators and determine the generalized connections. We show that this mega-space current algebra geometrically embeds the heterotic Chern--Simons structures into the generalized vielbeins and curvatures. We also show that the Green-Schwarz anomaly cancellation condition follows from the Jacobi identity for the algebra of stringy covariant derivatives, the ``nachos'' operators $\triangleright_{\mathcal{M}}$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies Lorentz and gauge connections in heterotic string theories within a manifest T-duality framework, motivated by the Bergshoeff–de Roo parallelism between torsionful Lorentz and Yang-Mills connections in heterotic α'-corrections. The authors formulate worldsheet current algebras in a "mega-space" incorporating both Lorentz and gauge sectors, generalize the Poláček-Siegel scheme to evaluate commutators of extended generators, and show that the mega-space current algebra geometrically embeds heterotic Chern-Simons structures into generalized vielbeins and curvatures. They further demonstrate that the Green-Schwarz anomaly cancellation condition follows from the Jacobi identity for the algebra of stringy covariant derivatives ("nachos" operators).
AI.motivation: The central motivation is the Bergshoeff–de Roo (BdR) type parallelism between the torsionful Lorentz and Yang-Mills connections in heterotic α'-corrections, which suggests a unified geometric framework that simultaneously incorporates both the Lorentz and gauge sectors within a manifest T-duality invariant formulation.
AI.method: The authors formulate worldsheet current algebras defined on a mega-space that simultaneously incorporates the Lorentz and gauge sectors. They generalize the Poláček-Siegel scheme (a framework for T-duality covariant current algebras) to evaluate commutators of extended generators, determine the generalized connections, and analyze the Jacobi identities for the algebra of stringy covariant derivative operators (nachos operators).
AI.result: The mega-space current algebra geometrically embeds the heterotic Chern-Simons structures into the generalized vielbeins and curvatures. The Green-Schwarz anomaly cancellation condition is shown to follow directly from the Jacobi identity of the nachos operator algebra.
AI.conclusion: The unified mega-space framework with manifest T-duality naturally accommodates both Lorentz and gauge connections in heterotic strings, recovering the BdR parallelism and deriving the Green-Schwarz anomaly cancellation from consistency (Jacobi identity) conditions, thereby providing a geometric foundation for heterotic α'-corrections.

title: Improved Approximations for Collective Neutrino Oscillations
summary: A one- and two-body $\mathfrak{su}(n)$ Hamiltonian governing the dynamics of many systems, including collective neutrino oscillations, is investigated. We start by analyzing the algebraic structure($\mathfrak{u}(n^N)$), formulate a product structure of the algebra, and utilize this to construct generic expressions for operator expectation values, Rényi Entropy, and Wigner Functions. Performing BBGKY hierarchy truncation we develop a systematic methodology for going beyond the mean field with polynomial scaling on a classical computer.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes a one- and two-body su(n) Hamiltonian (relevant to collective neutrino oscillations), develops a product algebra structure based on u(n^N), derives generic expressions for operator expectation values, Rényi entropy, and Wigner functions, and uses BBGKY hierarchy truncation to go beyond mean-field theory with polynomial classical computational scaling.
AI.motivation: To understand and simulate many-body quantum systems governed by su(n) Hamiltonians, such as collective neutrino oscillations, beyond the limitations of mean-field approximations, using classical computation with polynomial scaling.
AI.method: The paper analyzes the algebraic structure (u(n^N)), formulates a product structure of the algebra, constructs generic expressions for observable quantities, and truncates the BBGKY hierarchy to systematically go beyond mean-field theory.
AI.result: A systematic methodology is developed for going beyond the mean-field approximation with polynomial scaling on a classical computer, enabled by the algebraic product structure and generic expressions for relevant physical quantities.
AI.conclusion: The proposed BBGKY hierarchy truncation methodology provides a tractable classical computational path to study correlations in su(n) many-body systems beyond the mean-field level.

title: Quantum Trigonometric Spin Ruijsenaars-Schneider Models from $K$-theoretic Coulomb Branches
summary: We quantize the trigonometric spin Ruijsenaars-Schneider model of $N$ particles each with $\ell$ spin states using the recently developed description of the classical model in terms of the $K$-theoretic Coulomb branch of the 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ quiver gauge theory for the necklace quiver with $\ell$ nodes of rank $N$. The main algebraic tool is an algebra of $L$-operators derived from abelianized monopole operators of minuscule charge, which turns the necklace quiver into an integrable spin chain by producing a family of commuting Hamiltonians. We show that the lowest Hamiltonian coincides with the first mode of the quantum determinant of the horizontal quantum loop algebra living inside the $K$-theoretic Coulomb branch algebra, whose Bethe subalgebra generates a maximal family of commuting Hamiltonians. Finally, we derive the commutation relations and quantum equations of motion of the quantized physical spin variables.

AI.tldr: This paper quantizes the trigonometric spin Ruijsenaars-Schneider model using the K-theoretic Coulomb branch of a 4d N=2 quiver gauge theory for a necklace quiver with ℓ nodes of rank N, constructing an L-operator algebra from abelianized monopole operators that yields commuting Hamiltonians, and connecting the lowest Hamiltonian to the quantum determinant of the horizontal quantum loop algebra.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to quantize the trigonometric spin Ruijsenaars-Schneider model by leveraging a recent classical description in terms of K-theoretic Coulomb branches of 4d N=2 quiver gauge theories, providing a rigorous algebraic framework for the quantum integrable structure of this model.
AI.method: The approach uses an algebra of L-operators built from abelianized monopole operators of minuscule charge on the necklace quiver, generating a family of commuting Hamiltonians. The analysis connects the lowest Hamiltonian to the first mode of the quantum determinant of the horizontal quantum loop algebra inside the K-theoretic Coulomb branch algebra, and derives commutation relations and quantum equations of motion for the quantized physical spin variables.
AI.result: The paper produces a family of commuting Hamiltonians for the quantized spin Ruijsenaars-Schneider model, establishes that the lowest Hamiltonian coincides with the first quantum determinant mode of the horizontal quantum loop algebra, and derives the explicit commutation relations and quantum equations of motion for the physical spin variables.
AI.conclusion: The quantization of the spin Ruijsenaars-Schneider model is achieved within the K-theoretic Coulomb branch framework, establishing a concrete connection between the model's integrable structure, the Bethe subalgebra of the quantum loop algebra, and the dynamics of the quantized spin degrees of freedom.

title: Interior zeros of supersymmetric indices
summary: A supersymmetric index has interior zeros ($|q|<1$) if and only if the arithmetic coefficients $δ(ν)$ underlying the supersymmetric zeta function grow exponentially at a rate set by the nearest zero. Each $δ(ν)$ follows from finitely many $q$-series coefficients, so interior zeros are detectable from the expansion alone and obstruct a free or s-confining infrared description, as we show for 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ $SU(2)$ SQCD. With a giant graviton expansion interior zeros are a finite $N$ effect, located by the energy of one giant graviton, verified for the $\mathcal{N}=4$ $U(N)$ Schur index.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that interior zeros (|q|<1) in a supersymmetric index exist if and only if certain arithmetic coefficients δ(ν) grow exponentially at a rate set by the nearest zero, and that these zeros can be detected from finite q-series coefficients. Interior zeros obstruct free or s-confining IR descriptions (shown for 4d N=1 SU(2) SQCD). Using a giant graviton expansion, interior zeros are a finite N effect located by the energy of one giant graviton, verified for the N=4 U(N) Schur index.
AI.motivation: To understand when a supersymmetric index has interior zeros and what physical implications these zeros have, particularly regarding whether a theory admits a free or s-confining infrared description.
AI.method: The paper connects the existence of interior zeros to exponential growth of arithmetic coefficients δ(ν) underlying the supersymmetric zeta function, showing each δ(ν) can be computed from finitely many q-series coefficients. It then applies this to 4d N=1 SU(2) SQCD to demonstrate obstruction of free/s-confining descriptions, and uses the giant graviton expansion to locate interior zeros as a finite N effect in the N=4 U(N) Schur index.
AI.result: Interior zeros are shown to be detectable from the expansion alone and obstruct free or s-confining IR descriptions. For the N=4 U(N) Schur index, interior zeros are verified to be a finite N effect located by the energy of one giant graviton.
AI.conclusion: Interior zeros of supersymmetric indices carry physical significance, signaling the absence of free or s-confining infrared descriptions, and can be understood and located through arithmetic coefficients and the giant graviton expansion.

title: Nonlocal four-fermion theory
summary:
In this work, we formulate and analyze a nonlocal four-fermion theory in which the usual Dirac operator is deformed by an entire nonlocal form factor. After introducing an auxiliary scalar field, we derive the mean-field effective action and the corresponding gap equation for the dynamical mass. A central technical point of the analysis is that the nonlocal form factor is a matrix function of the Dirac operator, so the inverse propagator must be treated as an element of the closed algebra generated by the identity and $
ot{\!p}$ operators, rather than as a purely scalar quantity. We obtain explicit expressions for the gap kernel for two representative choices of a form factor, $f_{I}(
ot{\!\partial})=e^{-
ot{\partial}/Λ}$ and $f_{II}(
ot{\!\partial})=e^{-i
ot{\partial}/Λ}$. Following the IR/UV matching method used in the recent Dirac-like nonlocal spinor theory [1], the momentum integral is split at an intermediate scale $M\ll Ω\ll Λ$, expanded analytically in the infrared and ultraviolet regions, and compared with the usual local NJL/Gross-Neveu result. We show that the hyperbolic form factor enhances the gap integral and lowers the critical coupling, whereas the oscillatory form factor suppresses it and raises the critical coupling. The finite-temperature and finite-density extension is formulated through Matsubara sums and a corrected contour representation, with the local thermal gap equation recovered in the limit $Λ	o\infty$.

AI.tldr: This paper formulates and analyzes a nonlocal four-fermion (NJL-type) theory with a deformed Dirac operator incorporating an entire nonlocal form factor. The authors derive the mean-field effective action and gap equation for dynamical mass, treating the inverse propagator as an element of the algebra generated by identity and the momentum operator. They analyze two representative form factors (hyperbolic and oscillatory), showing the former enhances the gap integral and lowers the critical coupling while the latter does the opposite. Finite-temperature and density extensions are formulated via Matsubara sums.
AI.motivation: To extend nonlocal fermion theories by considering a deformed Dirac operator with a nonlocal form factor, and to understand how different choices of entire form factors affect dynamical mass generation, gap structure, and critical coupling compared to the standard local NJL/Gross-Neveu theory.
AI.method: The Dirac operator is deformed by an entire nonlocal form factor. An auxiliary scalar field is introduced to derive the mean-field effective action and gap equation. The inverse propagator is treated as an element of the closed algebra generated by the identity and the momentum operator (not a scalar). Two specific form factors are analyzed: f_I = e^{-∂/Λ} (hyperbolic) and f_II = e^{-i∂/Λ} (oscillatory). The IR/UV matching method splits the momentum integral at an intermediate scale M ≪ Ω ≪ Λ for analytic expansion in both regions, then compares with local NJL/Gross-Neveu results. Finite-temperature/density extension uses Matsubara sums with a corrected contour representation.
AI.result: Explicit gap kernel expressions are obtained for both form factors. The hyperbolic form factor enhances the gap integral and lowers the critical coupling, whereas the oscillatory form factor suppresses the gap integral and raises the critical coupling. In the Λ→∞ limit, the local thermal gap equation is recovered for the finite-temperature/density case.
AI.conclusion: The type of nonlocal form factor qualitatively changes the dynamical mass generation behavior: hyperbolic (real, damping) form factors strengthen symmetry breaking by enhancing the gap and lowering the critical coupling, while oscillatory (complex phase) form factors weaken it. The framework unifies the treatment of nonlocal Dirac operators in a consistent algebraic setting and reduces to standard local results in the infinite cutoff limit.

title: Light-Front approach to $4d$ massless Higher-Spin interactions
summary: This thesis studies $4d$ massless higher-spin interactions in the Light-Front approach by analysing the closure of the Poincaré algebra at quartic order. We first solve the light-cone quartic holomorphic constraint in flat space and show the existence of infinitely many interacting local higher-spin theories with either a finite or infinite number of fields. We classify all one- and two-derivative theories, corresponding to higher-spin extensions of gauge and gravitational interactions. These are consistent subsectors of higher-spin extensions of self-dual Yang--Mills and gravity, themselves truncations of Chiral Higher-Spin Gravity. We then clarify the relation between the OPE associativity in celestial CFT, the vanishing of tree-level amplitudes for generic kinematics, the Jacobi identity of the associated ''gauge algebra'' (kinematical algebra), and the light-cone holomorphic constraints. Finally, we investigate the non-holomorphic quartic constraint involving both MHV and anti-MHV vertices. We recover the existence of Yang-Mills theory and gravity, and the inconsistency of interacting multi-graviton theories. We then show that once higher-derivative cubic vertices are included, nontrivial solutions to the full quartic constraint exist. We classify all unitary local higher-spin theories, identify new families of local quasi-chiral theories, and determine all local higher-spin four-point amplitudes using the spinor-helicity formalism together with locality in the form of consistent factorisation.

AI.tldr: This thesis analyzes 4D massless higher-spin interactions using the Light-Front approach, solving the Poincaré algebra closure at quartic order. It classifies all unitary local higher-spin theories, identifies new families of local quasi-chiral theories, and determines all local higher-spin four-point amplitudes via spinor-helicity formalism and consistent factorisation.
AI.motivation: To understand and classify consistent interacting higher-spin theories in four dimensions, which are constrained by the closure of the Poincaré algebra, and to clarify the connections between different consistency conditions (OPE associativity, Jacobi identities, and light-cone holomorphic constraints).
AI.method: The thesis employs the Light-Front approach, solving the light-cone quartic holomorphic constraint in flat space. It classifies one- and two-derivative theories corresponding to higher-spin extensions of gauge and gravitational interactions, relates OPE associativity in celestial CFT to tree-level amplitude vanishing and Jacobi identities, and investigates non-holomorphic quartic constraints using spinor-helicity formalism with locality via consistent factorisation.
AI.result: Infinite families of interacting local higher-spin theories exist (finite or infinite field content). All one- and two-derivative theories are classified as subsectors of Chiral Higher-Spin Gravity extensions. Yang-Mills and gravity are recovered, multi-graviton interactions are inconsistent, yet nontrivial solutions exist once higher-derivative cubic vertices are included. All unitary local higher-spin theories and local four-point amplitudes are classified.
AI.conclusion: The Poincaré algebra closure at quartic order provides a powerful constraint for classifying higher-spin theories. Beyond Yang-Mills and gravity, including higher-derivative cubic vertices permits new consistent local quasi-chiral higher-spin theories, which are fully classified along with their four-point amplitudes.

title: Missing Descendants in the Carrollian Conformal Family
summary: In the Carrollian conformal algebra, the relation $[P^0,K^0]=0$ implies that $K^0$ annihilates all operators generated from a primary by temporal translation $P^0$. The standard conformal family defined by translation descendants does not contain the independent descendant chain that $K^0$ lowers successively to the primary. We construct the complete Carrollian conformal representation by including this chain together with all of its translation descendants. We derived the corresponding local operators, orbit structures, and checked their Casimirs in 2D and 3D. For each orbit configuration, the global two-point Ward identities fix the kinematic factors and selection rules for both magnetic non-contact branches and electric contact branches. Unlike ordinary conformal symmetry, Carrollian conformal symmetry generally determines the correlators only up to arbitrary functions of Carrollian invariants rather than constants. The complete representation contains sectors with $\mathcal{C}_2=m^2=κρ-β^2>0$ for 2D and $\mathcal{C}_2=m^2=κρ-\vecβ^{\,2}>0$ for 3D, which may describe massive states in flat holography.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs the complete Carrollian conformal representation by including the K^0-descendant chain alongside standard translation descendants, deriving local operators, orbit structures, and Casimirs in 2D and 3D, with global two-point Ward identities fixing kinematic factors and selection rules. The correlators are determined up to arbitrary functions of Carrollian invariants, and the representation contains positive-Casimir sectors potentially describing massive states in flat holography.
AI.motivation: The standard Carrollian conformal family built only from translation descendants is incomplete because [P^0,K^0]=0 implies K^0 annihilates all P^0-generated operators, missing an independent descendant chain lowered successively by K^0. The authors aim to construct the full representation and its correlator structure.
AI.method: The authors explicitly construct the complete Carrollian conformal representation by supplementing the translation-descendant family with the K^0-lowering chain and all its translation descendants. They derive local operators and orbit structures, verify Casimirs in 2D and 3D, and use global two-point Ward identities to fix kinematic factors and selection rules for magnetic non-contact and electric contact branches.
AI.result: The complete representation includes sectors with C2=m^2=κρ-β^2>0 in 2D and C2=m^2=κρ-|β|^2>0 in 3D, potentially describing massive states in flat holography. Unlike ordinary conformal symmetry, Carrollian conformal symmetry determines correlators only up to arbitrary functions of Carrollian invariants rather than constants.
AI.conclusion: The complete Carrollian conformal representation fixes the independent K^0-descendant chain that standard construction misses, and the resulting global Ward identities determine correlation functions up to arbitrary Carrollian-invariant functions, with positive-Casimir sectors offering a candidate description of massive states in flat holography.

title: Covariant variation and its applications
summary: We define a covariant variation of tensor fields by combining its Lie derivative with the metric variation. This operator preserves the metric, contractions, and Hodge duality, but its commutator is not closed due to an anomaly. We derive its algebraic and geometric properties, and compare it with the Kosmann derivative. Combining the covariant variation with Kosmann derivative gives total covariant variation for the fields with both spacetime and Lorentz structure, all of which belong to the metric Lie derivative. Moreover, we introduce families of extended operators which contain the affine connection, Lie derivative, and covariant variation. From the anomaly of the covariant variation along the superrotation, an electromagnetic helicity flux appears at null hypersurfaces in four dimensions. We also apply the covariant variation and its anomaly to tensor fields in arbitrary spacetime dimensions, and especially focus on the $p$-forms in $d=2p+2$ dimensions.

AI.tldr: The paper defines a covariant variation operator for tensor fields by combining Lie derivatives with metric variation, proving it preserves metric, contractions, and Hodge duality while exhibiting a non-closed commutator due to an anomaly. It introduces extended operator families and connects the anomaly to electromagnetic helicity flux at null hypersurfaces in four dimensions, with applications to p-forms in d=2p+2 dimensions.
AI.motivation: To construct a covariant variation operator that maintains key geometric properties (metric preservation, contractions, Hodge duality) while providing a useful alternative to existing derivatives like the Kosmann derivative, with applications to gauge theories and gravitational physics.
AI.method: The covariant variation is defined by combining the Lie derivative with metric variation. The paper derives its algebraic and geometric properties, compares it with the Kosmann derivative, and introduces families of extended operators containing the affine connection, Lie derivative, and covariant variation. Applications are studied via the anomaly structure along superrotations and for p-forms in d=2p+2 dimensions.
AI.result: The covariant variation preserves the metric, contractions, and Hodge duality, but its commutator is not closed due to an anomaly. Combining it with the Kosmann derivative yields a total covariant variation for fields with both spacetime and Lorentz structure. The anomaly produces an electromagnetic helicity flux at null hypersurfaces in four dimensions, and results extend to arbitrary spacetime dimensions with focus on p-forms in d=2p+2.
AI.conclusion: The covariant variation provides a new, well-behaved differential operator for tensor fields, and its anomaly has physically significant consequences (helicity flux at null hypersurfaces), with broad applicability across dimensions and field types.

title: Hayden--Preskill recovery at finite temperature on a quantum processor: dynamics and initial state from the SYK model
summary: In the original Hayden--Preskill recovery, the post-injection scrambler and initial state are {\it not related}. We extend this setup in two ways: by using a SWAP gate so that the scrambler and initial state are {\it related}, and by considering recovery at {\it finite} temperature. For this modified protocol, we show that the information is successfully recovered in the sense that the postselection probability is non-negligible and the conditional fidelity is large. We find that both the postselection probability and the conditional fidelity are proportional to temperature, reflecting the reduced entanglement of the initial state at lower temperatures. We also derive their late-time analytic estimates under the assumption of uniform operator spreading and show that they agree well with the numerical results. This demonstrates that strong scrambling is important for successful information recovery. Implementing the protocol on an IBM superconducting processor using a binary sparse SYK Hamiltonian with $N = 8$ Majoranas, we observe that the data retain the qualitative recovery dynamics and that a SWAP-based error-mitigation scheme improves both the postselection probability and the conditional fidelity.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the Hayden-Preskill recovery protocol by introducing a SWAP gate that relates the scrambler and initial state, and by considering finite-temperature recovery. The authors analytically and numerically show that both postselection probability and conditional fidelity scale with temperature, derive late-time estimates under uniform operator spreading, and validate the protocol on an IBM superconducting processor using a sparse SYK Hamiltonian with N=8 Majoranas, including a SWAP-based error-mitigation scheme.
AI.motivation: The original Hayden-Preskill recovery setup assumes the post-injection scrambler and initial state are unrelated. This work aims to generalize the protocol by making them related via a SWAP gate and by extending recovery to finite temperature, thereby probing how temperature and scrambling affect information recovery.
AI.method: The authors modify the Hayden-Preskill protocol by inserting a SWAP gate to relate the scrambler and initial state, and consider finite-temperature initial states. They derive late-time analytic estimates assuming uniform operator spreading, and compare with numerical results. They also implement the protocol on an IBM superconducting processor using a binary sparse SYK Hamiltonian with N=8 Majoranas, employing a SWAP-based error-mitigation scheme.
AI.result: Both the postselection probability and conditional fidelity are found to be proportional to temperature, reflecting reduced entanglement of the initial state at lower temperatures. The late-time analytic estimates agree well with numerical results. Hardware experiments on IBM's superconducting processor retain qualitative recovery dynamics, and the SWAP-based error mitigation improves both key metrics.
AI.conclusion: Successful information recovery depends on strong scrambling, as evidenced by the agreement between theory and numerics. The protocol works at finite temperature and on real quantum hardware, with error mitigation providing meaningful improvements, demonstrating the practical viability of Hayden-Preskill-type recovery.

title: Soft charges and zero modes at null boundaries
comment: To appear in Proceedings of Science for the Conference School "Foundations of General-Relativistic Gauge Field Theory" held at Politecnico di Torino, Italy, in March 2026
summary: Asymptotic symmetries at null boundaries provide a powerful window into the soft sector of field theories, revealing conserved charges and infinite-dimensional symmetry algebras beyond the standard bulk dynamics. While these structures are usually associated with residual gauge transformations, null boundaries also exhibit a characteristic global zero-mode ambiguity, whose physical consequences are less explored. We discuss how this zero mode modifies the canonical structure of field theories at null boundaries. In particular, we show that it gives rise to a new quasilocal edge observable, with consequences to the charge algebra. It can arise on any kind of null boundaries, both at the null infinity and the finite distance such as a black hole horizon.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a previously under-explored global zero-mode ambiguity at null boundaries in field theories, showing it modifies the canonical structure and gives rise to a new quasilocal edge observable that affects the charge algebra at both null infinity and finite-distance boundaries like black hole horizons.
AI.motivation: While asymptotic symmetries at null boundaries are well-studied in connection with residual gauge transformations, the physical consequences of the characteristic global zero-mode ambiguity at these boundaries remain largely unexplored.
AI.method: The authors analyze the canonical structure of field theories at null boundaries, demonstrating how the global zero mode modifies the symplectic structure and induces a new quasilocal edge observable. They argue this is a general feature applicable to all types of null boundaries, including null infinity and finite-distance boundaries such as black hole horizons.
AI.result: The zero mode gives rise to a new quasilocal edge observable that has consequences for the charge algebra. This mechanism is universal across all null boundaries—both at null infinity and at finite distance (e.g., black hole horizons).
AI.conclusion: The global zero-mode ambiguity at null boundaries is physically significant, introducing new edge observables and modifying the charge algebra. This provides a new window into the soft sector of field theories that extends beyond the usual treatment of residual gauge transformations.

title: Learning to Trace Seiberg Dualities
comment: 59 pages + appendices, 38 figures. Code and tools available at https://github.com/alexmininno/GNN-Pathfinders
summary: Dualities play an important role in establishing both microscopic and emergent phenomena in a wide range of physical systems. In practice, though, it can often be computationally challenging to establish when two systems are dual, even when all of the "rules of the game" are well-known. Said differently, when confronted with two systems, how can one efficiently establish that they are in fact dual? In this paper we use machine learning methods to address this question for Seiberg dualities of supersymmetric quiver gauge theories. Mathematically, this involves establishing mutations of quivers, which is in turn a variation on the theme of "learning to unknot". On the one hand, this leads us to a practical tool for establishing the computational complexity of different dualities. On the other hand, it also allows us to study how different network architectures learn how to trace Seiberg dualities. We find that for quivers with a modest number of quiver nodes (of order $10$), different network architectures consisting of transformers and multi-layer perceptrons tend to outperform deterministic algorithms. Supplementing the network by well-established pathfinder algorithms (essentially "Google Maps for quivers") leads to an additional improvement in the efficiency and accuracy of the search strategy. We anticipate that this class of questions can serve as a useful benchmark for frontier AI models applied to theoretical physics.

AI.tldr: The paper uses machine learning methods (transformers and multi-layer perceptrons) to establish Seiberg dualities of supersymmetric quiver gauge theories, framed mathematically as quiver mutations. For quivers with ~10 nodes, these network architectures outperform deterministic algorithms, and supplementing them with pathfinder algorithms further improves efficiency and accuracy.
AI.motivation: Dualities are central to physics, but computationally establishing when two systems are dual is challenging. The authors aim to address the question of how to efficiently verify duality in supersymmetric quiver gauge theories, which reduces to establishing quiver mutations—a variation on "learning to unknot"—and to assess the computational complexity of different dualities.
AI.method: Machine learning methods are applied to detect Seiberg dualities in quiver gauge theories. This is framed mathematically as quiver mutation detection. Different network architectures—specifically transformers and multi-layer perceptrons—are trained and compared against deterministic algorithms. Additionally, well-established pathfinder algorithms ("Google Maps for quivers") are used to supplement the networks to improve search efficiency and accuracy.
AI.result: For quivers with a modest number of nodes (~10), transformer and MLP network architectures outperform deterministic algorithms in establishing dualities. Supplementing the networks with pathfinder algorithms yields additional gains in efficiency and accuracy of the search strategy.
AI.conclusion: This class of duality-detection questions can serve as a useful benchmark for frontier AI models applied to theoretical physics, and the hybrid approach of neural networks augmented by pathfinding provides a practical tool for tackling duality problems.

title: The Conformal Origin of the Lepton Flavor Mixing Matrix
summary: Using the formalism of the flavor spin theory, we re-derive the TM1 lepton flavor mixing factor decomposition in a novel way, using a previously unreported near identity involving the elements of the first row of U_PMNS. The resulting mixing matrix is a direct consequence of the conformal symmetry of the massless SM before the EW phase transition. In addition to the previously reported results, we derive a relation between the CP violating phase and the three mixing angles. Application of the relation to the experimental data data suggests the TM1 decomposition should use (19/12)Pi as the value for the CP violating phase.
